working.detail: 104 people live in a local authority the need figures list. 6 live outside England and Wales, or in a local authority the figures do not list.

working.title: Set the area to compare
working.detail: Area: England and Wales. No catchment was given, so every local authority in England and Wales is compared. 104 of the 104 people located live in it, in 5 of its 8 local authorities.

working.title: Set reach against need
working.detail: For each local authority, the people you helped were divided by the people in need and multiplied by 100. A local authority is high need when its count of people in need is at or above the middle value of the area (8,500).

working.title: Listed the places with high need and low reach
working.detail: The 4 high-need local authorities were put in order of reach, lowest first, and then by need, highest first. The first 3 are listed. A hidden count is ranked as 4 people, the most a hidden small count can be.

working.title: Hid small counts
working.detail: Counts from 1 to 4 for a named local authority were hidden, along with anything that would let them be worked out. 2 cells or figures were hidden.

checks.question: Does each count stand for people, with nobody counted twice?
checks.why: The counts are added up as they are.

checks.question: Is the location where each person lives?
checks.why: Need is counted where people live. A postcode for a service, school or hostel would put people in the wrong place.

checks.question: Does the data cover the period you are reporting on?
checks.why: The lens cannot tell which dates the rows are from.

checks.question: Is this the need you work on: Unemployed women aged 16 to 64, not counting full-time students?
checks.why: Reach is only meaningful against the people you are trying to help. Change the 'need' option if another measure fits better.

checks.question: Is this the area you could serve: England and Wales?
checks.why: A place you could never reach is not a gap. Name the area with the 'catchment' option.

caveats: Low reach is not the same as unmet need. Another organisation may already serve a place where you reach few people.
Need is a count of people, so a large local authority is more likely to be listed as high need than a small one with the same rate.
Reach sets the people you helped against everyone counted as in need. The people you helped may not all be in that group.
The need figures describe census day, 21 March 2021. Unemployment was affected by the pandemic then and has changed since. Full-time students who were looking for work are not counted.
warnings: 1 rows named a local authority that the need figures do not list. Use the names or codes that Nomis uses.
6 people were placed outside England and Wales, or in a local authority the need figures do not list (for example one whose boundary has changed). They are left out.

notes: A count is hidden when it is small and is about a named local authority.
A hidden count is not always small. When only one count in a table is small, a second is hidden with it, so the first cannot be worked out from the total.
The map shows reach in bands, and the lowest band holds places with nobody and places with a hidden count.
The need figures are public counts and are shown in full.
